deadline_label: Must be enrolled before Day 1 of work
non_obvious_official_guidance: All employees in Germany earning below the Versicherungspflichtgrenze (approx. €69,300/year) are required to enrol in statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung).
non_obvious_actual_reality: German employer cannot register an employee for payroll without the Mitgliedsnummer. If the employee arrives without enrolling, Day 1 payroll is blocked — no workaround. Most major Krankenkassen (TK, AOK, Barmer) accept online international pre-enrolment before the employee sets foot in Germany.
non_obvious_action_required: HR sends Krankenkasse shortlist to employee at least 2 weeks before move date. Employee enrolls online and provides Mitgliedsnummer to HR before Day 1. HR confirms it is in payroll system before first payroll close.

deadline_label: Within 14 days of taking up residence — legal hard deadline
non_obvious_official_guidance: All persons taking up residence in Germany must register their address (Anmeldung) at the local Bürgeramt within 14 days under Bundesmeldegesetz § 17.
non_obvious_actual_reality: 14 days is a hard legal deadline with potential fines. Bürgeramt appointment availability in Berlin or Munich can be 3–6 weeks out. Employees who search for appointments after arriving face a structural problem. Many Bürgerämter have unpublicised early morning walk-in slots (7:30am). Berlin has allowed online Anmeldung in some districts since 2023. Required document often missed: Wohnungsgeberbestätigung (landlord confirmation letter) — without it the Anmeldung is rejected on the day.
non_obvious_action_required: HR warns employee of 14-day deadline and the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung requirement before the flight. Employee books Bürgeramt appointment online before arriving. If no appointments: check walk-in slots at 7:30am. Employee brings originals: passport + completed Anmeldeformular + Wohnungsgeberbestätigung.

source: Standard employer payroll practice (required for tax registration)

deadline_label: Arrives by post 2–3 weeks after Anmeldung — not requestable online or in-person
non_obvious_official_guidance: Upon Anmeldung, the Finanzamt automatically issues a Steueridentifikationsnummer (TIN) sent by post to the registered address within 2–3 weeks.
non_obvious_actual_reality: There is no way to expedite the Steuer-ID. You cannot call to receive it verbally. You cannot collect it at any office. It is posted to the registered address only — if the employee used a temporary address and then moved, the letter is lost permanently. Without Steuer-ID, employer must deduct highest tax rate (Lohnsteuerklasse VI). Employees routinely waste 2 weeks trying to 'request' it before discovering it's fully automated and postal.
non_obvious_action_required: HR warns employee before move: Steuer-ID arrives 2–3 weeks after Anmeldung, by post, to the REGISTERED address only. Employee must not change registered address until letter arrives. HR chases employee to confirm receipt and loads Steuer-ID to payroll before second payroll close.

deadline_label: Issued automatically via employer's first payroll submission
Must be granted before employment start — no right to work without it
